subject: Federated control-plane proposal for Nova private VPC

Subject: Federated control-plane proposal for Nova private VPC

Hi all,

Attached is our initial proposal for a federated control-plane option for Nova's private VPC deployment. High-level goals: keep the data plane (in-customer racks) fully isolated, minimize cross-site control traffic, and provide single-pane operational visibility from Redwood while allowing Nova to retain local control for ingress/egress policies.

Key points in the attachment:
- Control-plane brokers (lightweight agents) run in each customer rack and talk to a regional control-plane aggregator via TLS with mutual auth.
- Aggregators are multi-AZ within Nova's VPC and forward only metadata and rollouts; no KV cache or inference traffic leaves the rack.
- Failover model: local agent promotes a standby locally if aggregator unreachable; we expose an ops endpoint for manual remediation and a read-only reporting feed to Redwood Console.

Attachments: federated-controlplane-diagram.vsdx, runbook-diff.patch

Open questions I want us to answer before the call on Monday:
1) Karthik - does the runbook patch cover our canary rollback steps for a local-promote?
2) Neha - do we need a signed attestation for egress-proofing here (SOC-style evidence) or is the read-only feed sufficient?
3) Jonas - will this design fit within Nova's stated BGP/MTU constraints (they called out 1450 MTU on their edge links)?

Thanks — proposing a 40-minute sync Mon 10am PT with Nova.

— Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Federated control-plane proposal for Nova private VPC

Monica,

Thanks for the doc — quick read-through. A couple of implementation questions / notes:

- Canary rollback: the runbook patch looks good but we should be explicit about KV cache staleness windows. Suggest adding a short step: on local-promote, invalidate KV cache and trigger a prefix-only warmup for 30s to avoid surprise tail-latency.
- TLS auth: recommend mutual TLS with certs issued by Nova's internal CA (we should avoid public CA for the aggregator-client channel). Will need certificate rotation notes in the runbook.
- MTU: 1450 is tight. Jonas, is kernel offload / jumbo frames possible across their fabric? If not we need to ensure protobuf framing doesn't exceed path MTU (suggest compressing agent protobuf payloads).

I pulled the diagram and left two small annotations — attaching inline comments to the VSDX.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: NOVA Cloud Solutions <eng-sales@novacloud.com>

Subject: Re: Federated control-plane proposal for Nova private VPC

Hi Monica / Karthik,

Thanks for the clear proposal — this looks promising. A few constraints from Nova infra:
- We cannot accept any long-lived outbound connections from customer racks to a managed service unless they terminate inside our peered VPC(s) — can the aggregator live in our account (we can provision an endpoint)?
- For compliance we need an explicit egress-proof mechanism that shows no inference payload leaves the rack. A read-only reporting feed is fine, but we'd like a signed attestation artifact (JSON with hashes + timestamp) after every rollout step.
- We run a restricted MTU of 1450 and do not support jumbo frames (confirming). Our ops wants to see connection retry behavior for transient link flaps — we prefer exponential backoff with capped jitter.

Can you add an appendix demonstrating the attestation JSON and an example of the aggregator deployment inside our VPC? Also, what are the HA expectations if an entire aggregator AZ fails?

My team is available Mon 10am PT for the sync.

- Priya N. (on behalf of Nova infra)
Sr. Solutions Architect, NOVA Cloud Solutions
eng-sales@novacloud.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Federated control-plane proposal for Nova private VPC

Folks — answered inline and added an appendix sketch in the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-FedCP-Proposal

- Aggregator location: yes, we can run the aggregator inside Nova's peered VPC as a set of regional ECS/EKS-managed services. That satisfies outbound policy and keeps control-plane traffic within Nova's network. We will provide an AMI/container bundle and IaC script for them to run.
- Attestation: sample attestation JSON attached below (snippet). We'll sign it with Redwood's KMS private key and include Nova's nonce to bind it to their rollout event.

--- attestation.json (example) ---
{
  "rollout_id": "roll-20260629-001",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-29T19:00:12Z",
  "rack_id": "nova-rack-12",
  "inference_payload_hashes": [],
  "control_plane_manifest_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "signature": "MEUCIQD..."
}

- HA: aggregator inside Nova's account should use multi-AZ target groups with cross-AZ replication of metadata store (we recommend an eventually-consistent store; local agents must be tolerant to short replication windows). If an entire aggregator AZ fails the remaining AZs will serve traffic; local agents will only do local-promote when all aggregators are unreachable for >90s. That threshold is configurable.

- MTU: since Nova confirmed no jumbo frames, we'll enable gzip compression on agent payloads and add a fragmentation-aware client that fragments protobuf frames to respect path MTU.

Next steps / action items:
- Karthik: incorporate the KV-cache invalidate + prefix warmup step and cert rotation notes into runbook-diff.patch.
- Neha: draft the minimal attestation evidence template (SOC-lite) and confirm with Security whether it's sufficient.
- Monica: schedule the Mon 10am PT sync and share the agenda (10, 20, 10 minute split: architecture, runbook, Q&A).

Jonas Weber
